models.title: Teaching example: variable electricity charge
models.summary: Demonstrates the return contract using an existing accounting definition and synthetic checks. Do not resubmit this as new curation.

relationship.original_equation: variable charge = purchased electrical energy × flat unit tariff
relationship.locator: This kit's synthetic accounting definition; no external publication claimed
relationship.translation_notes: The unit price is constant over the same accounting interval as the electricity quantity. This example duplicates electricity-cost@1 to teach the format.

variables.definition: Purchased electricity in the stated representative annual interval
Constant real USD variable charge per purchased kWh
variables.domain: Nonnegative finite price; excludes export and negative-price regimes

variables.definition: Variable electrical operating cost over the matching interval

assumptions: A flat real tariff applies to all purchased electricity in the same representative annual interval.
limitations: Excludes fixed charges, maintenance, export compensation and negative tariffs.

sources.title: Synthetic flat-tariff accounting definition for the curation kit
sources.evidence: Multiplying a purchased quantity by its constant unit price defines the variable charge. This is an explicitly authored accounting identity, not an extracted empirical finding.
sources.license: Project-authored teaching fixture; no external quotation
sources.redistribution: Contains only this original short explanation and synthetic numerical inputs

references.method: Count twenty quarter-dollar charges: four quarters make one dollar, so five dollars total. Inputs are synthetic.

models.inverse_notes: Cost and a positive tariff determine energy. Zero tariff and zero cost leave energy underdetermined. Do not add separately published rearrangements.
